transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-08-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Laura Martinez (CISO, Greenfield), Ben Carter (Platform Eng), Rita Singh (IT Ops)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — go over SSO SAML setup, SCIM provisioning, RBAC mapping and then Q&A. uh Priya will run through the technical bits.
[00:20] Laura Martinez: Thanks Alex. to give you context, we're moving from Okta standard to a consolidated SSO flow for all third-party apps. main asks are: can we do IdP-initiated and SP-initiated, how do groups map to roles, and what's the deprovisioning guarantee.
[00:35] Priya Nair: Yep, we support both IdP-initiated and SP-initiated. on SAML specifics — we exchange metadata XML, we support certificate rotation, and we recommend using the entityID + NameID (email) as the primary assertion. small caveat: if you use persistent NameID formats we need mapping keys.
[01:05] Ben Carter: For group mappings, do we do SCIM group push or read groups in assertion?
[01:12] Priya Nair: We prefer SCIM push for group provisioning — more reliable for large orgs. SCIM is push-based from your IdP to our SCIM endpoint. group membership changes are synced near-real-time; there is also a periodic reconciliation job. note: some IdPs have rate limits so we'll discuss throttling.
[01:38] Rita Singh: How about deprovisioning SLA? if someone leaves, how fast is access revoked?
[01:45] Priya Nair: For push-style SCIM deprovisioning we see it happen within seconds to a few minutes — depends on IdP latency. we also have a background reconcile (every 15 minutes) that catches any missed deletes. we can also trigger on-demand full sync during the POC.
[02:05] Laura Martinez: Are there audit logs exposed? we need to ship logs to our SIEM (splunk) and have an immutable audit trail for user activity and role changes.
[02:14] Alex Chen: Yes — we emit admin and auth audit logs. retention defaults to 90 days for hosted, longer available as an add-on. Exports: S3 export or forward to Splunk/Datadog via syslog/HTTP. logs include SAML assertion events, SCIM provisioning API calls, session starts, model-run access events (note — can be noisy).
[02:40] Ben Carter: On the subject of retention — we operate under HITRUST/HIPAA concerns. we need logs in-region and for at-rest encryption.
[02:50] Priya Nair: Understood — we have region selection for hosted accounts. you can choose eu-west-1 or us-east-1 etc. encryption at rest is AES-256, and for customer-managed keys we support AWS KMS CMKs (bring-your-own-key) and HSM-backed keys for private deployments. we can provide KMS key rotation guidance.
[03:12] Laura Martinez: Great. Is traffic TLS-only? any mTLS option for the control plane?
[03:20] Priya Nair: All ingress is TLS 1.2+ and we support mTLS for private deployments and for some dedicated endpoints. for hosted we have standard TLS and client certs available for dedicated customers.
[03:33] Rita Singh: For SAML we need to test with our dev Okta tenant first. what's the normal metadata exchange?
[03:40] Alex Chen: We'll share our SP metadata XML — that contains ACS URLs, entityID, and cert. you can import it into Okta. if you want IdP-initiated flows, we just need the IdP metadata back. we'll also provide a step-by-step guide and a validated checklist.
[03:58] Ben Carter: Any gotchas for NameID or email as the primary key — some of our users have non-company emails in legacy accounts.
[04:05] Priya Nair: We can support alternative attribute mappings like employeeID or a custom attr, but employeeID needs to be unique across your userbase. we'll send the attribute mapping recommendations. note: mis-mapped attributes are the most common POC friction.
[04:30] Speaker 2: (inaudible) question on SCIM attribute mapping — can we map custom groups to roles?
[04:36] Priya Nair: Yes. SCIM supports group membership and custom group schemas. our RBAC supports mapping group X -> role admin/dev/audit via the RBAC template. during POC we'll provide a sample mapping file.
[04:55] Laura Martinez: For RBAC: what are the canonical roles you recommend for least privilege?
[05:00] Priya Nair: Typical roles: Org Admin (full), Platform Admin (deploy/config), Developer (create/consume endpoints), Auditor/Viewer (read-only), Billing (cost visibility only). we recommend start with Viewer+Dev, then escalate to Admin for a small set. we also support custom roles with scoped permissions.
[05:27] Ben Carter: Do you support attribute-based access control (ABAC) or just group-based RBAC?
[05:33] Priya Nair: Today we primarily support role & group-based RBAC plus some tag-based scoping on projects. ABAC is on the roadmap; however custom roles + groups covers most enterprise needs now.
[05:50] Alex Chen: On compliance — Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report and ISO readiness documentation. we'll share the SOC 2 summary and the redacted report under an NDA.
[05:59] Laura Martinez: We have legal review — NDA is fine. we also need to know about penetration testing cadence and vulnerability disclosures.
[06:07] Priya Nair: We do annual third-party pen tests and internal vuln scans more frequently. we also have a CVE triage and patching SLA for critical issues. we can share the summary page.
[06:20] Rita Singh: Regarding audit logs, can we get raw events associated with model invocations? like which token, which user triggered inference — PII concerns?
[06:30] Priya Nair: Audit logs include request metadata, user email, request ID, model name, and timestamp. we do not include raw customer prompt content in admin audit logs by default — that's treated as application data and subject to retention policies. you can enable full request logging for POCs if required, but that's gated by compliance and privacy review.
[06:55] Ben Carter: KMS integration — for hosted, if we bring our own CMK in KMS, can Redwood perform envelope encryption using the customer key?
[07:05] Priya Nair: Yes, we support envelope encryption with customer-managed CMKs for data-at-rest. keys stay in your KMS and Redwood gets encrypted blobs. for Private deployments you can bring an HSM-backed key for maximum control.
[07:22] Alex Chen: Quick note on data residency — you can pin to region, and for some regulated customers we offer Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) with a customer-managed control plane.
[07:34] Laura Martinez: That would be in our must-have list if we proceed to Dedicated or Private for PHI.
[07:40] Alex Chen: Absolutely — our sales team will scope Dedicated pricing separately.
[07:46] Ben Carter: On SCIM throttling — if we have 50k users will Redwood accept bulk provisioning?
[07:53] Priya Nair: We handle bulk via chunked SCIM ops. large orgs usually do an initial bulk load (CSV import or bulk SCIM calls) during onboarding, followed by incremental SCIM push. we'll coordinate a migration plan.
[08:10] Laura Martinez: What's the expected downtime patch window and maintenance notifications?
[08:16] Alex Chen: We give a 72-hour notice for disruptive maintenance. for minor patches we notify via the console and email. SLA for uptime is in Dedicated contracts; hosted is tracked via status page and SLAs for Dedicated.
[08:32] Rita Singh: Can we restrict API keys to IP allowlist and route-based permissions?
[08:38] Priya Nair: Yes — API keys can be scoped to routes and we support IP allowlisting for dedicated endpoints. for hosted we offer token scoping and short-lived keys with rotation best practices.
[08:52] Speaker 3: (crosstalk) what about SCIM attribute names — do you require enterpriseUser or userName?
[08:58] Priya Nair: userName is required as the primary unique identifier in SCIM. we accept enterprise extensions for custom attributes. we'll provide a sample SCIM schema.
[09:10] Laura Martinez: next steps recap?
[09:14] Alex Chen: Sure. we'll send SP metadata and SAML guide, SE to share RBAC template and SCIM schema, Greenfield to provision dev Okta tenant and invite our test account, then schedule a SCIM POC test call. also share SOC 2 report under NDA.
[09:34] Ben Carter: sounds good.
[09:36] Alex Chen: Any other immediate blockers?
[09:39] Laura Martinez: none from security side; legal will follow on NDA.
[09:43] Rita Singh: ops team will schedule time for the POC.
[09:46] Alex Chen: thanks all. we'll follow up with the artifacts in 48 hours.

End of transcript.
